answer: Delayed-Entropy Identity Windows.** New identities must wait through a fixed sequence of coordination rounds before gaining full weight, with each round's required participation quota rising toward a public nadir of free capacity. An attacker creating N identities must supply real coordination work in every window, so the per-identity cost scales with N times the round count, not a one-time fee. The design treats cheap coordination as a fable: apparent early activity earns no weight. Auditors post a copper deposit per challenged identity, refunded only if the window's work is verified.
